summary: Version-anchor mismatch during staggered regional rollout causing intermittent routing to legacy replica
description:
Issue summary: During a staggered regional canary rollout that should preserve a customer's per-route version-anchor, a subset of traffic was routed to the legacy (previous) model replica in a different region. Impact: Novum Analytics observed inconsistent responses and degraded quality for ~12% of requests to /v1/chat with model pinning enabled between 02:15–03:20 UTC. Some sessions received older-model outputs (shorter answers, different tokenization) leading to downstream validation failures.

Environment: Production, Dedicated capacity for Novum Analytics; regions impacted: us-east (primary), eu-west (canary). Models: raven-1.4-q8 promoted to canary in eu-west; rwd-infer-2.1-opt is currently pinned for Novum's route. Customer reported on 2026-03-11 02:45 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Customer config: route-level version_anchor: rwd-infer-2.1-opt, rollout policy: regional-staggered, canary weight=10% in eu-west.
2) Promote raven-1.4-q8 as canary in eu-west-only.
3) Generate steady-state traffic from us-east and eu-west test clients with session affinity and observe routing decisions and model IDs in response headers.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent routing decisions returned model_id: rwd-infer-2.1-opt (expected) and model_id: raven-1.4-q8 (unexpected) for the same customer route and session token.
- When routing to raven-1.4-q8, payloads sometimes differed structurally and triggered downstream schema validators to fail.
- Affected requests include both new sessions and established sessions — not limited to newly-created session tokens.
- Time-correlated with a burst of autoscaler activity in eu-west (spot preemption events logged 02:10–02:20 UTC).

Expected behavior: All requests for Novum's pinned route should stay on the anchored model unless an explicit rollback or unpin is performed. Canary traffic should only apply to unpinned or global routes, or be explicitly targeted via traffic-splits that respect anchors.

Logs & trace excerpts (sanitized):
- req=7b9f2a model_assigned=rwd-infer-2.1-opt route=novum/analytics session=ae3f
- req=7b9f2b model_assigned=raven-1.4-q8 route=novum/analytics session=ae3f
- routing_snapshot:route_key=novum/analytics anchors=[rwd-infer-2.1-opt] canary_weights={eu-west:10%}
- routing-cache-ttl=45s cache_miss=12% cache_invalidate=2026-03-11T02:11:09Z

Initial hypothesis:
- Routing cache invalidation is racing with per-region rollout markers. When eu-west autoscaler preempted spot instances, routing-controller emitted an immediate delta and cache invalidations propagated unevenly to frontends in us-east, temporarily exposing a fallback path that matched a regional canary replica.
- Another possible contributor is sticky-session metadata replication lag (session affinity changes not replicated quickly across frontends), allowing a different frontend with updated routing table to assign canary models for the same session.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Support applied a temporary route override (force_anchor=true) for Novum's route across regions at 03:25 UTC to unblock production traffic. Observed error rate dropped to baseline after the override.

Impact & customer communication:
- Customer-facing severity elevated to P1. We notified Novum Analytics at 03:40 UTC, applied the override, and offered a post-incident review. Customer requested logs for 02:00–04:00 UTC and expressed concern about future scheduled rollouts.

Next steps / required actions:
- Engineering to trace cache invalidation propagation paths and confirm TTL/sequence semantics for region-aware rollouts.
- Validate session affinity replication and consider hardening replication or using stronger version anchoring metadata in session tokens.
- Add telemetry for model-assignment divergence (per-session model_id drift rate) and create an alert if >1% drift for pinned routes.
- Schedule rollback of canary promotion until invariants are proven in cross-region scenarios.

References:
- routing PR suspected: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1987

comments: 2026-03-11 03:42 UTC — Asha Patel (Support): Notified customer of temporary route override (force_anchor). Asked for example request IDs and timestamp range. Customer confirmed 7b9f2a/7b9f2b among problematic requests.

2026-03-11 04:05 UTC — Martin Zhou (SRE): Observed routing-cache invalidations flooding after eu-west spot preempts. Created routing snapshot from 02:08–02:30 UTC and attached to internal investigation. Suspect race between cache invalidation and region-marker propagation.

2026-03-11 09:18 UTC — Ella Gomez (Engineering): Reproduced divergence locally with a test harness that simulates two-region frontends and delayed cache invalidation. Found case where sequence numbers were equal and a later-applied canary marker superseded anchor checks on a per-front-end basis.

2026-03-12 11:02 UTC — Support (Asha): Customer requested a postmortem and mitigation plan. Offered dedicated rollout window and ability to disable cross-region canaries for pinned routes. Novum accepted the rollback and requested additional SLA credit as goodwill.

2026-03-13 15:30 UTC — Martin Zhou (SRE): Plan to add a guard in routing-controller: never apply canary assignment if route has version_anchor flag set; also adding stricter cache-coherence checks. PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1994
resolution: Workaround applied (force_anchor=true). Engineering to implement guard in routing-controller and improve cache-coherence. Postmortem and formal mitigation scheduled.
